family B: trend in the logit of prevalences   trend_ols = list(label  = "Trend in logit prevalence (OLS)",                    method = "trend",                    col    = "#0072B2", lty = 1,                    args   = list(estimator = "ols")),    trend_end = list(label  = "Trend in logit prevalence (endpoints)",                    method = "trend",                    col    = "#56B4E9", lty = 1,                    args   = list(estimator = "endpoints")),    # family C: link with mortality (age shift k set to 0)   mort_common = list(label  = "Mortality link (common slope)",                      method = "mortality",                      col    = "#332288", lty = 1,                      args   = list(slope = "common")),    mort_byage = list(label  = "Mortality link (slope by age)",                     method = "mortality",                     col    = "#AA4499", lty = 1,                     args   = list(slope = "by_age")),    # family D: shift of the curve of prevalences   shift = list(label  = "Age shift",                method = "shift",                col    = "#8C564B", lty = 1) ) # Prevalences by age (60 to 104) projected with one specification. #   spec      : one element of `specs` #   fit_years : years used for the estimation #   new_mort  : table (year, age, qx) with the mortality of the projection years # Ages 100 to 104 are only used to compute life expectancies. predict_pix <- function(spec, fit_years, new_mort) {    years <- sort(unique(new_mort$year))    # Benchmark: the prevalences of the last year of the estimation, repeated for each year   if (spec$method == "constant") {     last <- pix99[pix99$year == max(fit_years), c("age", "pix")]     p <- do.call(rbind, lapply(years, function(y) data.frame(year = y, last)))     return(extend_ages(p))   }    # Table used for the estimation, which depends on the method   tab <- switch(spec$method,                 target    = tab_target,                 mortality = tab_mort,                 tab_trend)    # Estimation (warnings on the short estimation period are not displayed)   model <- suppressWarnings(     do.call(fitPrevalenceModel,             c(list(tab = tab, method = spec$method, fit_years = fit_years), spec$args))   )    # Mortality of the projection years: the method "target" works on the whole life table   # (60 to 104), the other methods on ages 60 to 99   if (spec$method == "target") {     newdata <- new_mort   } else {     newdata <- new_mort[new_mort$age <= 99, ]   }    # Projection; prevalences outside the interval 0 to 1 are bounded   p <- suppressWarnings(predict(model, newdata, on_unfeasible = "clip"))   p <- p[, c("year", "age", "pix")]    # Extension to ages 100-104, except for "target" which already covers them   if (spec$method != "target") {     p <- extend_ages(p)   }    p }   # Life expectancies (Sullivan method) from projected prevalences and mortality with_le <- function(p, new_mort) {   p <- merge(p[, c("year", "age", "pix")], new_mort, by = c("year", "age"))   CompleteDFLEtable(p) }   # Number of beneficiaries by year: sum over ages 60 to 99 of prevalence times population #   p    : projected prevalences (year, age, pix) #   popt : population (year, age, popx) count_beneficiaries <- function(p, popt) {   m <- merge(p[p$age <= 99, c("year", "age", "pix")],              popt,              by = c("year", "age"))   tapply(m$pix * m$popx, m$year, sum) }

title: Projects prevalences of disability and calculates life expectancies — projectPrevalence
code: # prevalences of the APA by single year of age, 2010-2024 (smoothing of the 6 age brackets, weighted by the population) apa <- FRAPAprevalence[FRAPAprevalence$decomp == 6, c("year", "age", "prevalence")] pop <- aggregate(popx ~ year + age0101, FRInseePopulation[FRInseePopulation$geo == "france" & FRInseePopulation$age0101 %in% 60:99, ], sum) names(pop) <- c("year", "age", "popx") pix <- ApproxPrevalenceTable(apa, agecuts = seq(60, 85, 5), agemin = 60, agemax = 99, weights.tab = pop, categories = "year") #> 'prevalence' is used as prevalence variable. pix <- data.frame(year = pix$year, age = pix$age, pix = pix$prevalence.approx) # extension up to age 104 (prevalence constant after age 99) pix <- rbind(pix, do.call(rbind, lapply(100:104, function(a) transform(pix[pix$age == 99, ], age = a))))  # mortality rates (Insee projections), the last age (104) having a mortality rate of 1 mort <- FRInseeMortalityForecast2026 mort <- mort[mort$sex == "all" & mort$geo == "France" & mort$def.age == "current age (approx)" &              mort$year %in% c(2025, 2030) & mort$age %in% 60:104, c("year", "age", "qx")] mort$qx[mort$age == 104] <- 1  # trend of prevalences at each age, estimated on 2010-2019, then projection and life expectancies res <- projectPrevalence(pix, newdata = mort, method = "trend", fit_years = 2010:2019) res[res$age == 60, c("year", "age", "pix", "ex", "DLEx", "pctDLEx")] #>    year age         pix       ex     DLEx  pctDLEx #> 1  2025  60 0.002573981 25.95770 2.397822 9.237422 #> 46 2030  60 0.002428811 26.31772 2.350002 8.929353 attr(res, "model")                  # the estimated model #> Model of prevalences by age, method "trend" (scale: logit) #>   Years used for the estimation: 2010 to 2019 (10 years) #>   Series: 1 #>   Ages: 60 to 104 #>   Estimator: ols #> Use coef(), as.data.frame(, what = ) and predict() to retrieve results and project prevalences.  # hypotheses on life expectancies need mortality rates in the estimation table too mort_obs <- FRInseeMortalityrates mort_obs <- mort_obs[mort_obs$sex == "all" & mort_obs$geo == "france" & !is.na(mort_obs$age) &                      mort_obs$age %in% 60:104 & mort_obs$year %in% 2010:2019, c("year", "age", "qx")] mort_obs$qx[mort_obs$age == 104] <- 1 tab <- merge(pix, mort_obs, by = c("year", "age"))  # uniform evolution of the prevalences at all ages, such that life expectancy with the APA at age 60 # follows its trend of 2010-2019 res2 <- projectPrevalence(tab, newdata = mort, method = "target", indicator = "dle", rule = "trend",                           scope = "min_age", fit_years = 2010:2019) res2[res2$age == 60, c("year", "age", "pix", "ex", "DLEx", "pctDLEx")] #>    year age         pix       ex     DLEx  pctDLEx #> 1  2025  60 0.002368359 25.95770 2.349853 9.052626 #> 46 2030  60 0.002158772 26.31772 2.296411 8.725720  # share of life expectancy lived with the APA, at each age, decreasing by 10 percent between 2019 and 2040. # (at the youngest ages, where prevalences are close to 0, the hypothesis can require slightly negative # prevalences: they are bounded to 0) res3 <- suppressWarnings(projectPrevalence(tab, newdata = mort, method = "target", indicator = "pct_dle",                          rule = "horizon", change = -10, horizon = 2040, on_unfeasible = "clip")) res3[res3$age %in% c(60, 85), c("year", "age", "pix", "DLEx", "pctDLEx")] #>    year age          pix     DLEx   pctDLEx #> 1  2025  60 0.0005170823 2.370714  9.132991 #> 26 2025  85 0.1737367725 2.730443 36.204274 #> 46 2030  60 0.0000000000 2.345566  8.912495 #> 71 2030  85 0.1645435766 2.728838 35.316915
